title: Bag-filter pulse-jet cleaning sequencer
nl_spec: A baghouse is cleaned by pulsing compressed air through three filter rows one at a time. A cleaning cycle starts from Idle when the filter differential pressure DP reaches DP_HIGH = 300 Pa OR a ManualClean request is made. The cycle is a fixed sequence: pulse row 1 (Valve1) for PULSE_TIME = 2 s, dwell 2 s, pulse row 2 (Valve2) for 2 s, dwell 2 s, pulse row 3 (Valve3) for 2 s, dwell 2 s, then return to Idle. At most one pulse valve may be energized at any time (simultaneous pulses would collapse header pressure). Model the sequence as an internal INT State (0 = idle, 1 = pulse1, 2 = dwell1, 3 = pulse2, 4 = dwell2, 5 = pulse3, 6 = dwell3) advanced by two TON timers (one for pulses, one for dwells). EStop is normally-closed (TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated); when activated the sequencer returns to Idle and all valves close. Write an IEC 61131-3 Structured Text PROGRAM named bag_filter with inputs DP, ManualClean, EStop and outputs Valve1, Valve2, Valve3.

interface.name: EStop
interface.description: Emergency stop, normally-closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated

safety_properties.nl: On emergency stop, all pulse valves are closed.
At most one pulse valve is energized at any time.
A pulse valve fires only while the system is healthy.
Positive obligation: in the row-1 pulse state, row-1 valve is energized.
Positive obligation: in the row-2 pulse state, row-2 valve is energized.
Positive obligation: in the row-3 pulse state, row-3 valve is energized.

scenarios.description: Trigger on high DP and pulse row 1 for two scans
Sequence advances through the dwell to pulse row 2
Emergency stop aborts the cycle and closes all valves
Full cleaning cycle: trigger on high DP, pulse rows 1-2-3 one at a time through all six active states, then return to Idle (DP dropped after the trigger so Idle is stable)

notes: DRAFT - pending expert PLC review. NEW FAMILY: cyclic one-at-a-time pulse sequencer with a header-protection one-hot invariant (at most one valve energized). Uses two TONs (pulse width + dwell) driving a 7-state CASE. Distinct from the existing linear start-up sequences (burner purge, conveyor start) which are one-shot ordered starts of persistent outputs; here the outputs are momentary, mutually exclusive pulses in a repeating cycle. The one-hot property is the novel class.
